forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Adur increases reserves by 37 per cent to strengthen finances
news_drafts.lead: Adur District Council has increased its reserves—money set aside for emergencies—from £14.2 million to £19.4 million, a 37 per cent rise. The improvement strengthens the council's financial cushion against unexpected costs and reflects investment income that exceeded budget because interest rates remained elevated longer than forecast. Adur's gross borrowing of £181.5 million stayed within its authorised limit of £254.8 million. Auditors noted potential capacity constraints in the shared finance team with Worthing Borough Council, which may affect the timing of 2025-26 audit procedures.
news_drafts.paper_title: Worthing BC 2025-26 Audit Planning Report Addendum

findings.paper_title: Worthing BC 2025-26 Audit Planning Report Addendum Appendix
findings.headline: Disclaimed audit opinion due to fundamental gaps in assurance over reserve classification and valuation
findings.detail: Worthing BC's auditor issued a disclaimed opinion on the 2024/25 accounts—meaning the auditors cannot vouch for them at all. The auditor explicitly states that gaps in assurance over how the council has classified its reserves are 'fundamental to user of the accounts given Worthing BC's financial position'. This follows a disclaimed opinion in 2023/24 and stems from the original disclaimer year of 2022/23. The auditor's focus for recovery is reserve classification and property, plant and equipment valuation, but recovery to a merely qualified opinion cannot happen before 2027/28 because the council values properties on a 5-year rolling cycle and properties from 2022/23 will not be revalued until then.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion means the auditors cannot assure the financial statements are accurate; a lender cannot reliably assess the council's true financial position, and the council itself has no audited confirmation of its reserves or asset values.
findings.figures: Properties last valued in 2022/23 would next be valued in 2027/28; 5 year rolling programme
findings.quote: the gaps in audit assurance over the classification of the Council's reserves, deriving from the disclaimers in prior years' was judged to be fundamental to user of the accounts given Worthing BC's financial position.

findings.paper_title: Adur DC 2025-26 Audit Planning Report Addendum Appendix
findings.headline: Audit opinion improved from disclaimer to qualified, but will remain qualified until at least 2027/28 due to asset revaluation timing.
findings.detail: The council received a disclaimer of opinion for 2023/24 and progressed to a qualified (except for) opinion for 2024/25. EY assesses this progress as in line with NAO guidance. However, the path to an unqualified opinion is blocked by the revaluation cycle for property, plant and equipment. Properties last valued in 2022/23 will not be revalued again until 2027/28, at which point the audit can move to unqualified.
findings.matters: Audit qualifications indicate limitations in the auditor's confidence in the financial statements' completeness and accuracy, which affects credit risk assessment and the reliability of the balance sheet.
findings.figures: 5 year rolling programme; properties last valued 2022/23; next valuation 2027/28
findings.quote: Therefore, we may not be able to move forward from a qualified (except for) opinion until that date.

findings.headline: CIL audit completed with Substantial assurance and minimal recommendations
findings.detail: The Community Infrastructure Levy audit was completed 16 June 2026 and received Substantial assurance with only 1 medium-priority recommendation. Substantial is the highest practical assurance rating, indicating effective controls.
findings.matters: Substantial assurance demonstrates well-controlled operations in at least one process area, providing evidence of effective control discipline in parts of the organisation.
findings.figures: Substantial assurance rating; 1 total recommendation (0 high, 1 medium, 0 low).
findings.quote: Community Infrastructure Levy ... Final Report ... 16/06/2026 ... Substantial ... 1

findings.headline: 35% of overdue audit recommendations remain incomplete, including 8 high-priority ones
findings.detail: As at 8 September 2026, of 128 recommendations that reached their due date, 83 have been closed but 43 (35%) remain in progress and not fully implemented. Of 17 high-priority recommendations, 8 remain in progress and uncompleted. The audit tracker was offline from 21 August, so status may not reflect current position.
findings.matters: Slow remediation of audit findings, especially high-priority ones, indicates weak control discipline and suggests the council lacks organisational capacity to remediate control weaknesses at the required pace.
findings.figures: Of 128 due: 83 closed, 43 in progress (35%), 2 not started. Of 17 high-priority: 9 closed/superseded, 8 in progress.
findings.quote: Of 128 actions that have reached their due dates, 83 have been reported as closed by management (Complete or Superseded) with a further 43 (35%) partially actioned (In Progress) and two not yet started.

findings.headline: Planned audit of Revenues & Benefits (core financial system) deferred because prior audit recommendations remain unimplemented
findings.detail: The audit of Revenues & Benefits was originally scheduled for 2026/27 as part of planned two-year coverage of key financial systems. However, it was deferred because prior recommendations are 'still being embedded'. Treasury Management audit was brought forward from long-term planning to replace it in the 2026/27 plan.
findings.matters: Key financial control systems require timely audit assurance; inability to audit Revenues & Benefits due to unresolved prior-year control weaknesses indicates slower pace of remediation and raises questions about the council's capability to implement control improvements promptly.
findings.figures: Revenues & Benefits deferred to December 2026 start; Treasury Management substituted in 2026/27 plan.
findings.quote: In planning, we were informed that Revenues & Benefits would need to be deferred due to some previous recommendations still being embedded.
